# Ring & Booked

> Ring & Booked provides a configured AI phone receptionist for service businesses. It is delivered as a done-for-you service: the Ring & Booked team works with each business to configure call handling, appointment booking, escalation rules, and caller-language preferences before launch.

## Official website

- https://ringandbooked.com/

## What Ring & Booked does

- Answers incoming business calls around the clock according to the rules approved by each business.
- Can write confirmed appointments into the business's Cal.com calendar.
- Can be configured to collect and structure caller details such as name, phone number, address, and requested service.
- Can be configured for call recording, transcription, and AI summaries where appropriate.
- Can be configured to route urgent calls to contacts selected by the business.
- Offers more than ten supported languages. The business chooses the languages needed for its callers, and the Ring & Booked team configures and tests those languages before the service goes live.

## Setup and trial

- Businesses submit onboarding information so Ring & Booked can configure and test the receptionist.
- Setup is done for the business rather than through a self-serve agent builder.
- The current site states that setup is typically live within one business day after onboarding, configuration, and testing.
- New accounts receive a seven-day trial that begins when the configured phone service goes live, not when an account is created or payment information is added.

## Plans and billing

- Starter: $89 per month, including 250 minutes.
- Growth: $189 per month, including 700 minutes.
- Enterprise: contact Ring & Booked for a tailored plan.
- Additional minutes are billed at the published rate of $0.35 per minute.
- Current monthly and annual billing terms are presented at checkout. Businesses can review subscription and cancellation information in the account workspace and the published policies.

## Important boundaries

- Ring & Booked is not an emergency-response, 911, utility-dispatch, medical, or safety-monitoring service.
- For an immediate emergency, callers should contact 911, the applicable utility, or local emergency services.
- Call recording, transcription, and summaries are configured with the business, including the applicable caller-notice and routing approach.
